description: Conformance fixtures for the F8 receipt-integrity signature profile. The positive pair must be accepted by the profile's rejection engine; every negative fixture must be rejected by exactly the rule set it declares in rejected_by. Status: PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED (v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA) — NOT IMPLEMENTED. Nothing here settles the ADR-0004 F8 deferral, authorizes a signer, or creates a runtime.
trust_bundle_note: This stands in for the pinned EXTERNAL trust bundle a verifier would resolve kid against. In the proposed profile the bundle is an operationally distributed artifact, never something a verifier fetches because a message told it to. Only the public JWK appears here; no private component exists anywhere in this repository.
test_only_key_disclosure: TEST-ONLY, NOT A SIGNER IDENTITY. The Ed25519 key pair behind this public JWK is derived at test runtime from SHA-256("CYBRIK-F8-TEST-ONLY-ED25519-SEED/v1"), so the private key is trivially recomputable by anyone and is worthless as a credential. That is deliberate: it makes the frozen vector byte-exactly reproducible without any PEM, PKCS#8 file, or secret in the tree. This kid must never appear in a real trust bundle. Production issuer, signer and key lifecycle are open prerequisites, not part of this proposal.

test_vector.note: One frozen receipt. It deliberately OMITS output_artifacts and input_artifact_digests, both of which carry `default: []` in the accepted cybrik.execution-receipt.v1 schema. The profile forbids materializing those defaults before hashing, and digest_evidence below is the proof that absence and an explicitly empty array are two distinguishable receipts.

digest_evidence.note: Two different digests for two different receipts. If the profile injected the schema default, a control plane that observed no output artifacts and one that observed an empty list would sign indistinguishable statements, and a verifier could not tell a receipt apart from a defaults-normalized rewrite of it. The absent digest is the one bound by the frozen envelope.

examples.invariant: The signed statement binds profile, profile_version, receipt contract id and version, canonicalization, receipt_id, receipt_digest, kid and signed_at — and nothing else.

Ordinary compact JWS with an included payload, EdDSA over Ed25519, protected header key set exactly {alg, kid, typ}, no embedded or remote key, locator equal to the SHA-256 of the exact compact JWS bytes.

The digest was produced by a bare JSON.stringify with no profile binding and the envelope declares that renderer. A non-JCS rendering, and any digest not reproducible under CYBRIK-RECEIPT-JCS/v1, must be rejected.
The classic alg=none downgrade with a stripped signature segment. Rejected as an algorithm violation, as a malformed compact serialization, and as an unverifiable signature.

The protected header carries the signing jwk, inviting a verifier to trust the message's own key. Rejected as a forbidden key-sourcing parameter, as a header key-set violation, and as an unverifiable signature.
The signed payload was re-bound to a different receipt_digest while the original signature and a correctly recomputed locator were kept, so only the cryptographic and payload-binding checks catch it.
